title: What India's New Minimum Support Price (MSP) for Kharif Crops Means for Your Wallet
description: The Indian government recently increased the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 14 Kharif (monsoon) crops for the 2026-27 marketing season. MSP is a guaranteed m.

faq.q: Which crops are covered under the recent Kharif MSP announcement?
faq.a: The recent announcement covers 14 Kharif crops, including paddy (common and Grade A), jowar, bajra, maize, tur (arhar), moong, urad, cotton, groundnut, sunflower seed, soyabean, sesamum, nigerseed, and ragi.

faq.q: How much has the MSP for paddy increased for 2026-27?
faq.a: For common grade paddy, the MSP has been increased by ₹72 per quintal, bringing it to ₹2,441 per quintal for the 2026-27 marketing season.

faq.q: What is the purpose of increasing MSP for crops like oilseeds and pulses?
faq.a: The government aims to encourage farmers to grow more oilseeds and pulses. This helps reduce India's dependence on imports for these commodities and promotes crop diversification.

faq.q: Does MSP apply to vegetables and fruits?
faq.a: No, MSP is not typically announced for perishable items like vegetables and fruits. It primarily focuses on staple food grains, pulses, oilseeds, and some commercial crops.

faq.q: How does MSP help with India's food security?
faq.a: By guaranteeing a minimum price, MSP encourages farmers to produce essential food grains. The crops procured by government agencies at MSP are then used to maintain buffer stocks and distribute food through welfare schemes like the Public Distribution System (PDS), ensuring food availability for citizens.
